paper_summary: ForkAudit presents an executable evidence contract for validating ownership isolation when a hybrid LLM forks continuations sharing token-indexed KV but carrying mutable GDN state. In one fixed Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/vLLM/Transformers configuration, it evaluates a 2x2 ownership factorial over N={1,8,32}, reports equality of registered outputs/states across 96 configurations, selected dense-attention and NumPy-GDN oracle checks, targeted live-fault reachability, and allocator accounting (Sections 3--5; Figure 3; Table 6). The paper is unusually candid that this is a bounded, conditional audit rather than a production serving claim. The central limitation is that the evidence establishes correctness only relative to producer-captured receipts, selected operator boundaries, and one sequential execution stack; it does not independently recapture the runtime or validate the compiled attention kernel, and terminal code-tree closure failed (Sections 3, 6--7; Table 9). Marginally below the acceptance threshold. The paper offers a thoughtful, transparent, and potentially useful audit methodology, with stronger controls than ordinary output-only tests. But the decision-driving evidence is too conditional for an executable audit contribution: source/provenance closure failed, compiled dispatch is not identified, independent checks start after candidate capture, and the evaluation remains a single sequential reference stack. A broader independently recaptured validation and restored artifact closure would materially change this assessment.
strongest_verified_contribution: The integration of lifecycle ownership witnesses, semantic relations, selected independent numerical oracles, fault-to-gate controls, and denominator-separated memory accounting into one explicit hybrid KV/GDN audit protocol, demonstrated on a controlled four-cell ownership factorial (Sections 3--5; Figure 2; Table 6).
strengths: The paper states a precise hybrid-state ownership problem and uses an appropriate factorial to separate KV-document sharing from GDN-base setup policy (Sections 3--4; Figure 2).
It distinguishes semantic equality, storage ownership, allocator values, and unmeasured device/service capacity rather than conflating memory metrics (Section 4.4; Table 6).
The paper avoids overclaiming performance: Table 4 labels CoMem's quality/state/latency tradeoff, and Table 5 explicitly avoids cross-framework speed comparisons.

Selected independent checks are stronger than cross-arm equality alone: eight dense-FP32 attention rows and four candidate-import-free NumPy GDN transition rows are reported with pre-fixed tolerances (Sections 5.5--5.6; Appendix Table 16).

The limitations are unusually explicit, including sequential execution, incomplete compiled-kernel provenance, targeted rather than complete mutation testing, and capture-bound replay (Sections 6--7; Appendix I).
questions: Can the authors provide an independently captured end-to-end trace or a second implementation/backend that validates at least one complete forked trajectory, rather than validating selected operators conditional on candidate-captured inputs? What failures would this additional check be designed to reveal?

What exact changes are needed to restore terminal code-tree closure, and can the final artifact bind the runnable source tree, environment, compiled-kernel/cache metadata, and raw receipts in one immutable manifest?

How does the ownership contract behave under concurrently executing CUDA streams, continuous/ragged batching, cancellation interleavings, and eviction/re-admission? Please test at least one such schedule or clearly narrow the title/abstract claims further.
Can the authors validate the contract on another hybrid architecture/runtime and at least one alternative KV precision/page geometry, with a predefined transfer criterion?

Why are selected attention rows and four GDN layers sufficient for the stated validation objective? Please provide a sampling rationale or expand coverage, particularly around the native q/k-normalization boundary that the GDN oracle intentionally excludes (Sections 5.5--5.6; Appendix I).

issues.observed_evidence: The audit's headline assurance is constrained by a trust boundary that is especially consequential here: its storage and semantic evidence is largely producer-captured hashes, and its independent numerical checks consume captured internal inputs. Thus replay can establish consistency of the supplied artifact but cannot independently establish that the original runtime path, upstream activations, or compiled kernel produced those inputs.
issues.why_it_matters: This is a substantive limitation for a paper whose contribution is an executable audit, not merely a localized implementation caveat.
issues.required_fix: Provide independently captured end-to-end traces or a second runtime/backend validation for complete forked trajectories.
issues.verification_test: Demonstrate that the independent capture/backend reproduces registered tokens, logits, state, and ownership predicates, and catches a predeclared set of representative faults.
issues.evidence_needed: Independent end-to-end validation that does not consume candidate-captured internal inputs, ideally through a second runtime/backend or independently collected trace.

issues.observed_evidence: The artifact identity guarantee is incomplete because terminal code-tree closure failed after the run. Calling pre-output identity "full" only within a narrowed derivative boundary is honest, but weakens the audit's core executable/provenance contribution.
issues.why_it_matters: The decision-driving evidence is too conditional for an executable audit contribution when source/provenance closure failed.
issues.required_fix: Restore terminal code-tree closure and bind the runnable source tree, environment, compiled-kernel/cache metadata, and raw receipts in one immutable manifest.
issues.verification_test: A clean replay from the immutable manifest should verify all source and environment bindings before reproducing every registered aggregate result.
issues.evidence_needed: A closed, immutable artifact binding source tree, environment, compiled-kernel/cache identity, raw data bindings, and replay results; specifically resolving the Section 7 terminal code-tree failure.

issues.observed_evidence: External validity is limited: one model and hardware family, one BF16 KV/page geometry, one partial-tail length, sequential round-major execution on one CUDA stream, and no continuous batching, scheduler behavior, eviction, or concurrent-kernel execution.
issues.why_it_matters: Validation on a single model, one page geometry, one sequential one-stream schedule, a non-optimized GDN path, and selected operator rows leaves uncertain whether the proposed audit materially generalizes beyond a carefully instrumented reference case.
issues.required_fix: Evaluate at least one additional hybrid model/runtime, another KV precision/page geometry, and one concurrent or batched/cancellation schedule.
issues.verification_test: Pre-register transfer criteria and show the ownership predicates, semantic-equivalence relations, and fault checks hold in the added configurations.
issues.evidence_needed: Pre-registered transfer results across at least one additional hybrid model/runtime plus concurrent/batched/cancellation schedules, showing the contract catches representative ownership faults without weakening semantic equivalence.

issues.observed_evidence: The deployment and serving tables are responsibly separated from the primary audit, but their volume and multiple caveats distract from the main claim and make the paper feel like several small studies rather than one sharply evaluated contribution.
issues.why_it_matters: The density of qualifications and many similarly named cohorts make the central novelty and assurance level harder to assess than necessary.
issues.required_fix: Condense the contextual cohorts or move more detail to the appendix, foregrounding the primary audit and its assurance boundary.
issues.verification_test: Readers should be able to identify the primary claim, supporting evidence, and non-pooled contextual results directly from the main results section.
issues.evidence_needed: A revision that clearly separates the primary audit from supporting context without changing the claim boundary.

issues.observed_evidence: The use of eight distinct books/ranks as workload sources rather than stochastic replicates and the absence of uncertainty estimates are acceptable for deterministic invariants, but should be foregrounded next to quantitative allocator and deployment claims.
issues.why_it_matters: Without this clarification, readers could infer statistical generality that is not measured.
issues.required_fix: State the sampling unit and determinism limitation next to each quantitative table, and add variability information where it is meaningful.
issues.verification_test: Revised tables should identify whether values are deterministic rank outcomes, repeated timings, or workload averages and should not imply unmeasured statistical generality.
issues.evidence_needed: Revised quantitative tables with explicit sampling-unit and variability annotations.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics issue is apparent from the PDF-only evidence. The work studies system behavior using the PG-19 training split and appropriately notes that it does not assess downstream safety, privacy, bias, or deployment impacts (Appendix A).
llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was generated with LLM assistance and is based solely on the permitted PDF and rubric.

dimension_justifications.soundness: The reported checks are internally coherent and their scope is carefully bounded. The factorial uses relevant ownership controls, checks non-vacuous request--base GDN disjointness at N=1, and separates logical-page and allocator denominators (Sections 4.1--4.5; Table 6). However, the principal correctness conclusion remains conditional on honest capture: most runtime values are hash receipts rather than retained tensors, the independent oracles begin from candidate-captured inputs, and dispatch provenance omits the compiled Triton binary and autotuning identity (Sections 3, 5.5--5.6, 6; Table 9). Further, the stated reproducibility boundary admits that post-ledger pycache files broke terminal code-tree closure (Section 7). These are substantive limitations for a paper whose contribution is an executable audit, not merely localized implementation caveats.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is well structured, defines claim boundaries repeatedly, and Tables 4--6 and Figure 3 make the principal results legible. It productively distinguishes the primary factorial from deployment, serving, Mac, and lifecycle cohorts (Sections 4--6; Appendix Table 8). Still, the density of qualifications, many similarly named cohorts, and the reliance on numerous appendical receipts make the central novelty and assurance level harder to assess than necessary. The repeated use of terms such as "full" alongside conditional capture/replay guarantees can also mislead a reader unless Table 9 and Sections 3 and 6 are read closely.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The integration of lifecycle ownership witnesses, semantic relations, selected independent numerical oracles, fault-to-gate controls, and denominator-separated accounting is a useful systems-testing recipe. The paper also clearly acknowledges that the component mechanisms are established prior art (Section 2; Appendix Tables 13--14). But validation on a single model, one page geometry, one sequential one-stream schedule, a non-optimized GDN path, and selected operator rows leaves uncertain whether the proposed audit materially generalizes beyond a carefully instrumented reference case (Sections 4.1--4.3, 6; Appendix I).

evidence_that_would_raise_score: A closed, immutable artifact binding source tree, environment, compiled-kernel/cache identity, raw data bindings, and replay results; specifically resolving the Section 7 terminal code-tree failure.
Independent end-to-end validation that does not consume candidate-captured internal inputs, ideally through a second runtime/backend or independently collected trace.

Pre-registered transfer results across at least one additional hybrid model/runtime plus concurrent/batched/cancellation schedules, showing the contract catches representative ownership faults without weakening semantic equivalence.
Expanded or principled sampled numerical coverage that includes the upstream q/k-normalization boundary and more GDN layers.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reproduce any registered cross-arm, storage-disjointness, fault-gate, or numerical-oracle result from the supplied receipts.
Evidence that the missing compiled-kernel/autotuning identity changes behavior while the callable ledger remains unchanged.
A source-tree or manifest discrepancy that makes the reported raw receipts unverifiable, or an ownership failure under an in-scope schedule claimed by the paper.
review_limitations: I evaluated only the frozen manuscript PDF and supplied ICLR rubric.
I did not inspect artifacts, code, prior reviews, author history, or revision materials.
